author: val
body: Pins the gauge fill and the input caret of apps/guios/GopRender inside their widgets. The instrument has to scan OUTSIDE the widget: an over-wide fill and a one-pixel caret are written exactly as correct ones are, so a reading that asks only whether either is present answers yes in both worlds. What distinguishes them is where the paint stops.

author: val
body: Each tree is the widget under test pinned to a fixed width with an empty label taking the rest of the row. A label emits text and no box, so nothing but the widget itself paints in the band to its right. The gauge is 150 of 100 because a value inside its maximum cannot discriminate a clamped renderer from an unclamped one. The input carries no text deliberately: caret and text draw in the same colour, so an outside hit against a non-empty input could be either.

author: val
body: Five readings, two of which are controls no defect here can move: gauge inside says the gauge painted at all, input box says the input painted at all. Without them a renderer that drew nothing would report a clean outside and pass. The other three are assertions and all three moved with the fix: before it they read gauge outside 1, input inside 0, input outside 1, measured against seed 6867EA9D.

author: val
body: A test under codex/test CAN cite an app quire: cites Guios chapter GopRender and cites Guios chapter GuiTimer both resolve, and there was no precedent for it in codex/test before this file. Rendering into a heap GopBuf via UI chapter PixelBuf rather than the framebuffer means no .vmargs is needed. gop-buf-hline clips to the BUFFER, so the buffer must be wider than the widget or the escape is invisible.
